proposal: The Mandate recommends that the next administration work with Congress to eliminate DOE's applied energy and demonstration programs, naming EERE, the fossil energy and carbon management office, the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, the Grid Deployment Office, the State and Community Energy Programs office and ARPA-E. Where an office survives, it should concentrate on fundamental science and energy security, and Congress should rescind excess unspent funds.
remaining: Congress would need to repeal or defund the statutory offices and programs (OCED and GDO were created under the IIJA; ARPA-E under the 2007 COMPETES Act); the FY2026 act zeroed OCED but continued to fund ARPA-E and EERE.

Rescind remaining unspent applied-energy appropriations; the FY2026 act transferred about 5.165 billion dollars of unobligated balances to other uses rather than rescinding them (CRS), and DOE's FY2027 request proposes cancelling 15.2 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds.
Narrow the retained energy technology, demonstration and appliance divisions to the basic-science and security focus the Mandate describes as its fallback.
Resolve litigation over the award terminations.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-17 DOE has reorganized most of the named offices out of stand-alone existence, but Congress has not eliminated them and kept funding several in FY2026. DOE's organization chart dated 2025-11-20 does not show EERE, the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, the Grid Deployment Office, the fossil energy office, the State and Community Energy Programs office, the Federal Energy Management Program or the Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains office as stand-alone offices; it shows a new Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, a Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office and ARPA-E as a stand-alone office. CRS describes EERE as renamed the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, the fossil energy office as renamed the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office and the Loan Programs Office as renamed the Office of Energy Dominance Financing, with OCED's duties divided among other offices. The FY2026 Energy and Water act is Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, approved 2026-01-23); per CRS and the House Appropriations Committee summary it gave EERE 1.950 billion dollars in new funds (1.510 billion below FY2025) plus 1.150 billion dollars of prior-year IIJA balances, ARPA-E 350 million dollars (110 million below FY2025), Fossil Energy 720 million and Grid Deployment 25 million, gave OCED nothing, kept the old account names, and transferred 5.165 billion dollars of unobligated balances to other uses rather than rescinding them. DOE's FY2027 request (April 2026) seeks 1.12 billion dollars for the renamed EERE office, 200.3 million for ARPA-E and nothing for OCED, and proposes cancelling 15.2 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds. DOE's page for the new innovation office, checked 2026-10-07, still lists a division for the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations and focus areas covering state and community programs, so much of the work continues under new names. DOE announced termination of about 7.56 billion dollars in awards on 2025-10-01, and a court vacated some cancellations in June 2026.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 directs agencies to pause disbursement of funds appropriated under the IRA and IIJA pending review, which affects the programs run by these offices.

DOE announces it has terminated 321 financial awards supporting 223 projects, with estimated savings of about 7.56 billion dollars, issued by OCED, EERE, GDO, MESC, ARPA-E and Fossil Energy, after a case-by-case financial review (DOE release); S&P Global reports the action came on the first day of a government shutdown.

DOE publishes an organization chart dated 2025-11-20 that does not show EERE, FECM, GDO, OCED, SCEP, FEMP or MESC as stand-alone offices; it shows a new Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, a Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office, an Office of Energy Dominance Financing and ARPA-E as a stand-alone office. Holland & Knight and Latitude Media describe where the programs moved, and DOE tied the changes to its energy dominance agenda.

The FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations act, Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938), is approved. Per CRS R48599 (updated 2026-03-25) and the House Appropriations Committee summary, it provides EERE 1.950 billion dollars in new funds plus 1.150 billion dollars of prior-year IIJA balances, ARPA-E 350 million, Fossil Energy 720 million and Grid Deployment 25 million, gives the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations nothing, and in Sec. 311 transfers 5.165 billion dollars of unobligated balances to other DOE uses; the Division B text itself was not readable.

DOE issues its FY2027 Budget in Brief (April 2026, month-only date): it requests 1.12 billion dollars for the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (formerly EERE), 200.3 million for ARPA-E, nothing for OCED and 676 million for the Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office (formerly Fossil Energy), and proposes cancelling 15.2 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds.
A federal judge in the District of Columbia vacates DOE's cancellation of 11 EERE grants worth 82.1 million dollars (date inferred from an article published 2026-06-12).
